Definition: a girding on (of the ephod); hence, generally, a plating (of metal)
BiblicalUsage: Ephuddah is the girding on of the ephod — the curious girdle of the priestly garment, woven of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and also the plating of metal over an idol. The same word covers the girdle of the high priest and the silver overlay of a graven image.
TheologicalSignificance: What is woven for worship and what is plated for idols can look alike, and the difference is whom it serves. I hold that the word warns me to ask the question about every fine thing in my life: is this girded for God, or plated for an idol?
